Same app.
Eight rendering configurations.

The minimal live Docker list, with the same Slint UI, Bollard client, fields, search and manual Refresh. Seven renderer-family builds cover eight runtime configurations, including Qt as a separate windowing/rendering backend.

Executable size excludes shared platform/driver libraries; Qt also excludes its system Qt libraries, so this is not bundled distribution size. The Qt run mapped libQt6 files totaling 47.76 MiB on disk, outside its executable; plugins and other dependencies are additional. This is not a complete bundle-size total. Window-visible time precedes the warmup and does not prove completion of the first rendered frame. The reference ID digest is 9b3587c9a02aefc52a6ad2b5c04fb1ba6e3615c0673b13bf87ce0bc1db2ff931.

What is controlled?

Every build uses the same 181-line application source, including its inline UI definitions. Cargo.lock pins the same Bollard/Tokio versions, and Slint is pinned at 1.18.1. The UI uses Fluent styling and a dark palette for every mode, including Qt. Docker requests run on a worker, with API negotiation, a 10-second request timeout and a 20,000-row post-decode retention check. No JSON input, Docker subprocess, polling or container mutations are used by the apps.

Each family enables only its corresponding renderer feature. Skia’s software/WGPU modes share one family binary. Skia/OpenGL uses a separate build with the explicit OpenGL feature; its size is reported independently. The Qt build uses system Qt shared libraries; executable size excludes those libraries and their dependencies. Other platform libraries and graphics drivers are excluded from ELF sizes too.

Native windows

Captures come from owned native windows after startup or after a measured interval. Startup and inventory are observed; search/Refresh interaction is not established by these captures. No automated test suite was added or run.

Rendering paths and interpretation

Slint software and Skia software explicitly select CPU rasterization. FemtoVG/OpenGL and Skia/OpenGL request the OpenGL path. FemtoVG/WGPU, Skia/WGPU and Vello request WGPU; the child environment requests Vulkan using WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan. Renderer names are explicitly selected, and unsuccessful configurations are retained as failures. WGPU modes also request the Intel adapter with WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME=Intel, which Slint’s WGPU initialization honors. The external GLX summary reports Intel Arc as the default OpenGL device; Vulkan lists both Intel Arc and NVIDIA RTX 500 Ada. This aligns the requested device family, but per-process adapter choice is not independently instrumented. Vello is experimental in this Slint release.

Qt is a different Slint backend, not merely a Winit renderer. Qt supplies its windowing/event/rendering integration. All runs use X11/XWayland at scale 1, with client size normalized to 1,000 × 680. No Wayland-native, Windows or macOS execution is claimed.

The original experiment compared different UI frameworks. This experiment holds the app and toolkit constant, making renderer overhead easier to assess. It still does not assign every allocated byte to the renderer: libraries, driver state, font caches, allocators, and platform integration contribute. RSS includes resident shared pages; PSS apportions them. Display-server/compositor memory and full GPU allocation are outside these process measurements.

For the current mostly static list, idle measurements do not demonstrate a GPU benefit. GPU rendering may help frequent redraws, terminal output, charts, animation or high-DPI scrolling, but active-use CPU/frame-time/latency measurements would be required to evaluate that. No such throughput claim is made here.

Same release profile: opt-level z, fat LTO, one codegen unit, panic abort, stripping, disabled unwind tables, four Cargo jobs, Fluent widget style. These are sequential development build observations with a shared warm cache. Newly required dependencies and prebuilt third-party downloads may be included; they are not comparable full clean-build or controlled source-edit timings. Build failures are part of the outcome.

Protocol and evidence

  1. Build every family and preserve each executable separately.
  2. Collect current full container IDs through a read-only external reference command.
  3. Launch each working configuration separately under strace for startup, socket/exec observation and a native capture; close its owned process group. These observations also warm renderer caches.
  4. Run three rounds in matrix order, one application at a time, with four seconds to settle and twenty seconds of RSS/PSS/CPU sampling every 500 ms. No compilation or strace runs during sampling.
  5. Compare all full IDs, capture after the measured interval, then close only the owned process group.
  6. Audit native logs for renderer fallback. The initial Skia/OpenGL request fell back because its explicit feature was missing. Exclude those measurements, build renderer-skia-opengl, then repeat its three runs separately. This corrected row is not interleaved contemporaneously with the other seven.

Renderer configuration: Slint 1.18.1 features. Sources and launch commands: experiments/live-docker/slint-renderers/README.md.
